title: Good but room for improvement
body: I would love to see weather metrics available in app as a factor for pain, particularly for trend analysis it’s an important variable. Additionally the statistics being used to determine trends seems somewhat questionable without seeing any of the BTS analyses - but from what I can see a required sample size of 3 for this kind of data seems to only be providing inaccurate results. For example according to my trends I have reduced pain when I 1) have my phone in the bed (this contradicts research), when I am sedentary (this I know makes my pain worse), and when I’m overthinking future events… these are obviously incorrect inferences from correlations of small samples. Since I’m paying so much for premium I expected that the trends at least make sense but now it’s impossible to tease out any true trends without more data. If I had to guess, the model being used isn’t accounting for excess zeros in the data due to people not logging a certain thing, so perhaps the days I was feeling worse were just when I started using the app and so as I started feeling better I added in more detail to the data. But you can adjust for this, and you should be using a ZIP or ZINB model - you shouldn’t be using basic correlation matrices for data this complex. And when it displays results for 2 days vs 1 day - is that dealing with the data collectively or analysing temporal trends? This app is great, and could be amazing if the results are useable.

title: What a wonderful health champion Bearable is!
body:

title: Super helpful app (and developers)
body:
I’ve used bearable for a few years now.
I have three overlapping chronic conditions and balancing treatments for each is difficult - this makes it much easier.
I find just the act of “paying attention” to how I am going each day is so helpful for my mental state; but also being able to look back at the data and find correlations has helped me figure things out that doctors missed.
Also, the developers go above and beyond. I have request feature changes or tweaks more than once, they have communicated with me to clarify what would help, then found a way to work that in without compromising how the app works for other users. An awesome, unheard of, level of customisation.

While I totally understand the price point and think it’s reasonably priced, unfortunately the cost of the premium features is a blocker for me. I’m on the free trial at the moment and am so sad that I know I won’t be continuing on the paid version as I genuinely can’t afford it long term due to ongoing and unpredictable medical costs ☹️ I’ve entered the Hero raffle, so fingers crossed!! ❤️ I love that this Hero functionality has been built for this app, it’s such an awesome idea and should be a guiding post for similar start ups! 

I really have never been so consistent with a health tracking app before and I really love its features, especially the insights. I’ve finally finished enough days that I can see the trends starting to form in the graphs and can already tell my habit forming is going really well. 

Love you Bearable!

Bearable has it all - all the features needed to see trends and find out what’s happening over time. Good looking (important), very few (if any) bugs, huge flexibility, easy to use, and actually fun to update. I love the graphs in particular. 

The fact that the free version isn’t really all that limited shows they really believe in their users and what they’re going through. The ability to sponsor others for a premium upgrade is also a very cool community feature. 

Just using this app I feel less alone.

title: Free version is ok :)
body: I love the idea of this, and even more I adore animals and there is a cute little bear to interact with so for me that’s a big draw lol. But, as someone who is happy to support devs, for me this one isn’t worth the sub price. I would pay a one time unlock right now, but would not feel the need to sub to this at its current cost. I found a few totally free apps that have even more depth (if you’re curious look for chronic health tracking apps produced by medical professionals) so I’ve picked a favourite of those and will track simultaneously in there as well as the free version of this app for now and see how I like it. I was surprised to find that even though I was logged in with my Apple ID I was not able to freely log in from both my iPhone and iPad. That feature isn’t supported and you have to constantly log in and out, making the process a bit of a chore. It’s been a long time since I’ve used an app that couldn’t be logged in on two devices. As someone who is disabled and needs to budget responsibly the yearly cost is just too high to justify right now, even if there is a cute little bear.

title: This app is a game changer
body:
As someone with multiple chronic conditions that impact each other and my life in complicated ways, Bearable turns out to be exactly what I need to better understand and manage my health. 

Like a lot of people with conditions that impact executive function, I have a really hard time building new routines and rituals, even if those are crucial to managing my health. So my current favourite feature (of many) are Bearable’s experiments—because being able to see concrete data on how behaviour or other changes are having a specific impact make it so much easier to stick with those changes. 

I also love that James and the team have lived experience with managing complex health conditions—it shows, and the app wouldn’t be half as good without that first-hand knowledge.

title: Neat, but ultimately useless
body:
I used this app for a full year. It’s great for helping you become more mindful of your symptoms, but ultimately kind of useless for finding how your daily actions and choices affect those symptoms.

One big problem is that the app has no notion of statistical power, so when showing correlations, something you might have done a handful of times is given equal weight to something you might have done hundreds of times. That is, the app shows the magnitude of a correlation, but not the likelihood that this magnitude is just a fluke.

author: Doesn't work 102020

title: Pretty comprehensive
body: Loving this app so far. I have been tracking food, symptoms, and sleep across three different apps for years—great to be able to do it all in one! Only two downsides I hope the developers will resolve. 1. Menstrual cycles don’t seem to be their own category—they’re either a “symptom” or a “factor.” Like nutrition and bowel movements, they should be their own category. Additionally, food has limited entries and no time-stamps. If I have more than one snack between meals, they both have to be logged in the same snack entry. And did I have that snack at 9am? 10:30am? No one knows! When relating symptom onset to food allergies/intolerances, time stamps become important. This is still better than using three apps, so I will continue to use this app for now.

PS: I love the presentation with colors, icons and font. Usually, there is enough space to write comments (both for items and notes). Well done!!

The gentle reminders you can set throughout the day so you won‘t forget to protocol your moods and overall health have been really helpful and it‘s also made it easier for me to be able to communicate to my therapist, what I feel throughout the day and what happened in a particular moment, that trigered me in certain ways. 
I would recommend this app to anyone who has been looking for an everyday help.

Also: I love the design of the app and the tiny notes you can make - especially what you are grateful for. It just gives you some positivity at the end of the day and time to think about the things that are going well in your life. 
Huge thank you to bearable for understanding what people like me need without having to pay a lot of money for it!

title: Makes me feel better.
body:
This is my preferred tool for tracking mental health and related factors. It has a nice and uncluttered interface which works well with my ADHD brain.

The gratitude journalling feature has subtly helped me to build better habits. So has the ability to see correlations between my mood with different good habits and maladaptive behaviours.

Even at its most basic, the ability to log my mood and see changes over time validates my feelings, gives me some hope in bad times, and makes me proud of the progress I have made.

Especially when taking medication, my mental health log reassures me that its effects are actually positive. I now feel quite secure keeping an eye on side effects.

There are a few additions I would like to see, eg. automatic weather tracking, but Bearable already stands out as its design and feature-set is so deliberately tailored.

title: Has potential, needs improvements
body:
I’ve used this app for a few months and it has a lot of potential and is one of the better health trackers available, but the Insights feature is held back by how it analyses data.

Everything seems to be grouped by calendar day, so symptoms that happen in the morning can end up being linked to factors that didn’t occur until later that day. This can create correlations that don’t make sense and makes it harder to trust the insights.

I’d love to see symptoms and factors analysed by time of day (morning, afternoon, evening, overnight) or with configurable time lags. That would make the correlations much more meaningful, especially for people with digestive issues, migraines, chronic illnesses or symptoms that fluctuate throughout the day.

If this was improved, I’d happily increase my rating because the rest of the app is excellent.

title: Saving my life.
body:
This app is incredible. An utter game changer. 

What I love most is that it functions perfectly well on the free version - because we shouldn’t have to pay even more as disabled people (who already face extra costs) just to track our health. But the premium options are there if you want them, and the hero scheme (where you can donate for others to get premium) is something I’ve never seen before but I think is the most wonderful idea!!! Especially in our community.

This app is seriously saving and changing my life. With invisible disabilities, I’m constantly doubting if what I feel is real. This app helps me track in an easy way and prove to myself that yes, this is real, and also spot patterns (like I always crash on a weekend, after pushing through the week). 

Seriously. Sending the biggest love to the creators of this app. I’ve recommended it at uni to student well-being for any other disabled students because WOW. 

PS: also, the fact that you can tailor it so much is incredible. Tracking bowel movements, etc - I’m in love with this app.
author: MorskoiMish

title: Daily driver
body:
I have used this app daily for 3 years. I love that I can tweak and refine what I’m tracking and see quickly correlations and insights. When you first start, it can feel a bit overwhelming but I soon made it my own. Over the years, it has been incredibly useful in tracking and uncovering insights as well as encouraging me to follow positive habits.

Every six months or so, I have been downloading the data and running it through some custom analysis (PCA, random forest, clustering, etc) and it’s been extremely useful to understand deeply what factors influence my wellbeing, productivity and how I can navigate around challenges. I’d love to see Bearable take on more of this deeper analysis (a great start would be clustering for day types) or simply to provide an easier-to-parse download format. 

It’s my most used app and my daily driver. Thoroughly recommend.

title: Not worth it
body:
I really regret paying for this.

1. App is an incredibly confusing interface and almost impossible to navigate, the analysis sections in particular are incoherent

2. You cannot track periods which seems bizarre given half the population has them. You can log them but they just vanish into the general mass of data with no clear way to retrieve them.

3. The app only logs correlations which makes most conclusions totally useless (for example it logs acute meds as harmful as they are taken on flareup days)

4. The app is inaccessible for disabled people as the interface is so badly visually and logistically designed and overcomplicated. The features are not clear. 

 
I will be looking for another app! Don’t waste your money!
author: jrjwjwjejdkrkrkrrkf

title: Essential if you have a chronic illness
body:
Really fantastic easy to use tool to track correlations and look at data around all aspects of health to work out what habits and interventions are helpful vs harmful. The data surprised me, the visualisations are great and it is an invaluable tool when communicating with my healthcare team to understand my symptoms. 

I have endometriosis which is a complex systemic disease involving lots of areas of the body- being able to give consistent data to different professionals involved in my healthcare has been beyond helpful. 

The only danger is maybe over analysing or collecting but what I love is the app does the analysis for you - all you have to do is track what is happening. It takes some time to figure out what’s useful to know vs not and you have to consistently track to get good correlations. 

Correlation doesn’t mean causation and I think the app developers could include a bit more guidance on interpreting this data in the future. 

I wouldn’t be without it, even a year after my last surgery! Now I track a lot less than I did pre and post op but it’s so helpful to see positive trends over time during a months long recovery.

title: Really great for tracking physical and mental symptoms!
body:
Having struggled with a very changeable auto-immune condition since my pre-teens, I have regularly been just “unwell” seemingly without rhyme or reason. Bearable lets me see the patterns (where there are patterns!) in my flare-ups or good spells and how they change with regard to what I’ve been doing or eating or feeling. 

It’s useful for me, but also for my medical team who’re working with me to find out if there are medications or procedures etc that can make things easier. 

As for feedback, being able to track “mild, moderate, severe, unbearable” is really useful, but I would appreciate a general guideline about what each of these represents.
For example, I’m usually in pain somewhere, so (for example£ my baseline pain is a 4 out of 10, so I’d say “mild” is more of a 5-6. A friend recently however commented that their “mild” would be a 2 and their “moderate” would be a 5. Apparently most typically healthy people have a baseline of 0 pain 😂

author: Aespdrum

title: Gamechanger
body:
This app is wild. It’s by far the most comprehensive symptom/health tracker, that somehow manages to accomplish its task without being patronising. Can’t say that about many tracking apps. 

I love the ability to customise factors and categories, it makes it incredibly useful, as health is always so specific to individuals. 

It also makes it easier for me to actually use the app because I can create custom only-I-know-what-I-mean moods and factors that I’m more likely to track (like “janky” lol) because sometimes looking at pre-existing words like “happy” or “anxious” doesn’t quite capture what you’re feeling, so you don’t select them. Also deleting them helps too, then the options don’t seem so personally out of touch, and don’t take up space on your screen. 

Also, having had GAD and PTSD since childhood, and a number of neuroendocrine disorders in adulthood, I’ve come to learn that symptoms like “anxiety” can feel completely different on different days. 

Some days it’s constant low-grade agitation and sensory sensitivity, some days it’s feeling vaguely numb and disconnected from life but in a way that’s hard to put your finger on, some days it’s a physically paralysing inability to get out of bed, even to eat or use the bathroom. 

The ability to fully customise increases consistent use of the app, which is imperative in data tracking. 

I love this app. I take a boatload of medications and supplements that I sometimes forget to take consistently, so it’s been illuminating to actually make inferences from what symptoms correlate to the times when I remember (or forget) to take various meds. 

I’ve also cured my acne that I’ve had for 15 years. Turns out I just needed an antihistamine. Who knew? 

Bearable knew. 

Thanks to the devs for making this app. It’s made health tracking finally feel engaging, and actually helpful, when it used to be the bane of my existence.

author: Disappointedreviewerlondon

title: ‘Beary’ good app!
body:
I’ve suffered with chronic pain/muscle tightness on my entire right side for over 6 years now and am on several medications to help cope with the pain. I’ve also been dealing with my fair share of stress and anxiety during my PhD which often exacerbates my symptoms. It’s safe to say this app has catered to all of the above issues! I love the Bearable app!! Many other apps are: ‘unBearable’; have terrible UIs; or are often unstable. Bearable on the other is nothing short of beautiful!! Rich features and an attractive UI make this app an enjoyable experience (I sound like an advert 😅). I’m obsessed with data visualisation and love how much data I can see about my own body and mind, without having to create them myself!

Feature requests:

- I wish the medication reminders nudged you once or twice more as it is easy for that notification to get lost in the Notification Centre.

- Although it auto tracks my Apple health data, these variables don’t seem to be included in the insights tab - other than sleep. It would be nice if these were built into the modelling i.e. steps and symptoms (or mood).

- I really enjoy using the app and this is more out of interest than anything, but I’m curious about some of the spurious correlations and whether things like multicollinearity are considered when providing insights?

Thanking you for a terrific app 🐻 👏🏻

title: Best mood tracking app out there
body:

Once customised, you can easily tap on a symptom and even rate its severity. I like that even when I’m in a low, the app is easy to use and intuitive so on the days I can’t get out of bed, I don’t lose valuable data that’s important for keeping on top of my health. I like that you can also break it down further and add multiple moods throughout the day which is really helpful for us rapid cycling folk, and also break down symptoms into times of day as well which may support other people with things like BPD or people looking to track their triggers for anxiety for example.
Absolutely fantastic app - couldn’t recommend more highly! Wish there was a 6 star option!!

title: Doesn’t work, programming wrong
body:

Like I take my anxiety medication when I have anxiety and it only says the medication makes my mood worse. The same with meditation or everything else I might do when I feel bad to make my self feel better. 

Also the mood points each day isn’t the best. If you feel great at 10 AND really bad at 1 one day, it says your mood was 5 that day. So it’s impossible to track mood swings. 
Also if you track that you feel really bad for most of the day, and then you feel better and then a little bit better for a short moment. It will say you felt good that day because you said you felt better two times and you said you felt bad one time. Even though you felt bad for soooo many more hours.

author: Calistang68

title: Extremely useful App
body:
I used Bearable in the past but didn't keep it up and kept forgetting, this is normal for me. I have all the common problems: Bipolar 1, depression,
ADHD, anxiety disorder, heart disease, blood clotting disorder, etc.

But since January I have been having symptoms that don't fit with those. I started trying to keep up with them, but kept forgetting. AND THEN, I remembered BEARABLE.

Being able to add any symptoms I'm having has made a huge difference!! I have a record to show the doctor. She was amazed. I had dates, timelines, symptoms, and everything that was different than usual, like I forgot to eat, how many trips to the ladies room, what I ate, my mood and as many as you need to add for your particular situation. The doctor ordered a MRI and appropriate blood test. I found out that I don't have what I thought but I was heard by my doctor.

Bear is easy to setup and use, even a reminder so you don't forget. It's worth getting and using.
The reports tell you and your doctor how you are doing.

title: Time consuming for little data feedback
body:
I've been using this app for two years, as a paid user for the first year. I initially started using it to test it out for someone with chronic health conditions who is taking about 30 medications per day. I've been using it to track my own medical conditions and mental health.

This app causes me more anxiety just to use it. It requires me to fill out dozens and dozens of symptoms at different ratings twice a day. That would be perfectly OK if I felt that I was getting good or even average interpreted information on the app that explained correlations of my symptoms. Hopefully that would in turn, allow me to know when I will have a flareup or know what factors to avoid that lead to increased symptoms.

My entire purpose of using the app is to hopefully understand how some of my symptoms correlate and to be able to reduce their severity. In terms of using it to track mental health symptoms, it's even more depressing to get through with a tough day and have an app that gives you absolutely no coping mechanism or positive messages for solutions to any of the symptoms that you're going through. Understandably, it is a tracking app and not a treatment app. 

The app has a lot of great customizability and features, however for my uses I have concluded after two years that it is not worth my time and I will return to my previous methods. My friend didn't end up downloading it either because they were not interested in having to fill out so much information every day.

title: The Best Health Tracking App I’ve Found
body:
I’ve tried a lot of health tracking apps over the years, and Bearable is by far my favorite. As someone living with multiple chronic illnesses, it’s incredibly helpful to have one place to track symptoms, pain, sleep, medications, mood, energy, vitals, and so much more.

What really sets Bearable apart is its flexibility. You can customize almost everything to fit your own health conditions and daily routine. I also love the insights feature, which helps identify patterns and possible triggers that I might never have noticed on my own. Those reports have been useful not only for me but also when discussing my health with my doctors.

The developers are constantly improving the app and genuinely listen to feedback from the community. If you’re looking for a powerful, customizable health tracker that can grow with your needs, I highly recommend Bearable. It’s become an essential part of managing my health. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

title: Supportive aid
body:
I can’t say enough good things about the Bearable app. As someone dealing with chronic pain and day-to-day health challenges, this app has genuinely been a game changer for me.

It’s incredibly easy to use, but also very detailed—you can track symptoms, mood, sleep, medications, and so much more all in one place. What really stands out is how it helps you start to see patterns over time. Things I never would have connected on my own suddenly make more sense, and that’s empowering.

It doesn’t feel overwhelming like some health apps can. Instead, it feels supportive—like a tool that’s actually built for people who are trying to understand their bodies better, not just collect data.

Honestly, it’s helped me feel a little more in control of my health, and that’s something I really needed. I would absolutely recommend it to anyone managing chronic illness, mental health, or even just wanting better insight into their daily wellbeing.

Other gripes:
- factors in the calendar view don’t include things like sleep quality or duration.
- lifestyle factors like alcohol, caffeine, etc are bucketed into ‘a lot,’ ‘a little’ etc which is how you report them, but to not be able to just overlay ‘alcohol’ as a concept vs having to do ‘alcohol: a little’ etc is just asinine. 

Overall just feels like this is built for vibey people to give them feely goodies and not for people actually interested in bio hacking and statistics. The features that would unlock a power user are not big tho, so idk what gives.

author: NiNi X3

title: Excellent - but with room to improve
body:
I needed a symptom tracker and wanted one with additional features I could use to record and understand my condition. Bearable fit the bill and I do believe it is the best option for me! It is very adaptable and granular, which are among many traits I love.
But I was slightly disappointed in a few ways others should consider before choosing this app...
I think its adaptability works against it in some cases, as the interface is rarely optimal for the current task. If there was a focused view that opened with the relavent notification, that would make things like logging meds a little faster (it does for check-ins but nothing else afaik). The check ins are also a little confusing and convolute with other features. But it's perfectly manageable, and I understand that this type of development is rightfully often a low priority.
Similarly, it is hard to make cumulative edits. If you accidentally enter data on the wrong date, which can be easy to do, there is no way to move/copy it other than manually.
Finally, I understood the app to have more in terms of task management and journaling. It sort of has both, but you get more of a routine/goal reminder than a to do list, and 'journaling' is in the form of optional (usually Premium) notes. These are also a "cherry on top" features, but I interpreted the description as including these.

It's a great app and I'm grateful for the developers! I give 4 stars considering that a good and honest rating. I believe these points are being addressed already, and I intend to update my review as features evolve.
author: I wrote this:

author: Mewveon

title: It’s good but not great
body:
Feb 27, 2026 Edit:
they’ve changed the format and now it’s way harder to add a one off symptom than it should be. this was a big one for me, because the one offs are more insightful at times than the daily things I go thru. I immediately cancelled my subscription. The kind of people using this app don’t have bandwidth to tinker with settings every time something changes. I don’t want to join discord or read the subreddit. I’m a Gen-Xennial with chronic pain - I just want the app to serve its purpose without complicating my existence.

Dec. 2025
My doctor asked me to start tracking symptoms so we can further narrow a few things down in my chronic illness journey. I’m too forgetful to go the notebook route, so the reminders to check in have been great and I love the customization capabilities for symptom tracking. If I could add anything to it, I’d like the ability to track symptoms thru the day - ie if my back pain starts at noon, I’d like to pop into the app and mark that down. Right now I get a pop up that says “This will mark (symptom) for all day - are you sure” (or something along those lines.)
I’d rather have a time stamp for when I entered the symptom like there are for other things the app tracks.
EDIT TO ADD: developer response helped me fix the timing issue - I missed that setting.
I would still like a fuller & more reliable integration with Apple Health. My watch tracks so many things that could feed into the app, but don’t.
Other than that - I’m a happy camper.

title: Easy to use, but privacy is a dealbreaker
body:
I used Bearable for well over a year and there’s a lot to like. The app is easy to use, the interface is friendly, and the tracking is fairly customizable. It’s a simple way to log symptoms and keep everything in one place.

That said, I was originally hoping for more meaningful insights. The correlations I got mostly confirmed things I already suspected, and over time the effort of recording symptoms every day started to feel like more hassle than it was worth.

What ultimately pushed me to stop using Bearable was privacy. My iPhone’s App Privacy Report showed the app regularly contacting a Facebook domain, even though I don’t use Facebook to log in. For a health‑related app, that’s a hard no for me. If the developers ever remove those trackers and take a more privacy‑first approach, I’d be open to giving it another try - but in its current state, I’m out.

title: LOVE this app (and want a little more)
body:
I love this app. It’s been very helpful in managing symptoms and treatment for my menstrual cycle, mental health, lupus and any other cold, pain or illness that comes up. It’s user friendly and offers a good deal of customization. I appreciate the reports it’s able to generate and will likely be using this app for a long time. That said, I’d love to see a few improvements especially around the medication tracking. It would be super helpful to: 
- be able to save dosage instructions for each medication in the app
- set reminders based on a set number of hours you have to wait before taking another dose. for example: if i mark having taken Tylenol at 11am, it could automatically set a reminder for me to take it again at 5pm. Or at least let me make a note on the medication for how often I can take it. 
- be able to set/save MAX dosing info (ie. I’ve taken 4 out of my allotted 6 Tylenol today)

In terms of tracking symptoms, it would be very helpful to be able to mark the time symptoms start / stop, worsen or change. 

And in terms of nutrition, having the option to track or at least save the amount of protein, fat, carbs, fiber, etc I’ve had during every meal / every day would be a game changer. So much of chronic illness deals with diet, I’d just love to see more capabilities here. 

All in all though- this app is amazing. I notice a huge difference in my discipline and overall health when I am consistently using it, and I will always recommend it to friends /family. My requests are simply geared towards allowing me to use this app MORE. If I could manage everything in one magical place (and have that place be Bearable), life managing everything would be just a weeeeeee bit easier 🙏🏾

author: LoveAGoodPod85

title: If You’ve Got The Time
body:
It’s definitely an all in one health care tracking app but it’s super complex and takes a lot of time to setup and then to do your check in two to three times a day. There’s a lot of complicated areas of the app and I would only recommend it to people who are really interested in tracking every aspect of their health journey. That being said it’s difficult to setup, missing options and limiting options on being better at tracking specific health issues. You really have to go out of your way to manually setup how you want to track the illness and it doesn’t really give you the ability to design a system around your specific disease. 

To be honest, I’d just stick to a handwritten journal if you want to really create your own system for tracking your very specific health care and plan, the mood you’re in, and so forth. This app just just is too complicated, takes a lot of time to setup, and doesn’t even offer ways to track side effects, tracking how you’re progressing, and for me I just don’t see the value in it with the amount of time it takes to get through your check ins or even offering everything you should track based on your health issue.

author: HeiheiBirdie

title: So helpful
body:
I love Bearable. When I first installed the app I chose to track basically everything I possibly could, but didn’t upgrade to premium. I tracked for about three months and didn’t look at any of my data because it was difficult to consume all the charts and graphs without the ease of premium telling me “your mood is generally worse when you have a migraine” and so on. Then I got premium in a Black Friday deal and have been amazed by the correlations Bearable has put together. I 100% recommend this app, and suggest you to track as much as you can! (Without getting stressed about it.) Taking time to do morning and evening check-ins every day for consistency has really changed my chronic illness journey as I’m able to see potential triggers and things that help. 
The only downside I can see to this app is that I haven’t found a way to track the local weather and how it may relate to your symptoms. I would love an update with this!
author: TheLonelyNerd

title: Pretty good - some UI suggestions for accessibility
body:
I LOVE the variety of options and wide customization so that I don’t need separate apps, however, the process of entering all of that data has become quite tedious.

It would be nice to have options to describe the qualities of the pain (like burning or sharp) and be able to select multiple locations (rather than having to have separate items for facial pain and hand pain). I use this app for most of the available features, so I think it would be nice to have an option to have different tabs for those aspects—and then select from a customized list of items—rather than have to create new ones and scroll down a long line of lists. I find the selectable options (as in your food tracking and mood tabs) much easier and quicker to use.

Also would much appreciate being able to send the data I input here to Apple Health, and being able to import my water data from Apple Health…and track amounts of drinks other than water.

body: So many chronic pain and illness apps are so laborious with a dreadful daily check-in interface that takes far too long to “log” your experiences. The interface is cute and not too clinical; it’d also be great for tweens or teens with chronic conditions. Highly recommend!
author: ZzzMouse_06

title: I don’t review things often…but this app is AMAZING!
body: I have been dealing with gallbladder, gallbladder, removal, surgery, and severe gastrointestinal issues for the last year. I am very young still at the age of 34. I have been waiting an appointment with a G.I. doctor for the last several months while my symptoms have continued to worsen and I’ve dropped a lot of weight, I am vomiting every day, amongst many other things. This is affecting my ability to work as well as I usually do because I am a workaholic through and through… Needless to say, I have been struggling pretty badly and have an already anxious predisposition when it comes to health issues. This app has single-handedly given me the ability to track my symptoms with such great detail that I am confident I will have a record of my symptoms to provide the G.I. doctor when my appointment happens in December. I decided to pay for the yearly upgrade, but even without that the free version was amazing! The insights that it provides is helpful while I’m able to use those insights to adjust my lifestyle which will be really helpful to share with the doctor so that they know exactly what I have tried and what I need more help with. I’m so self-conscious sharing how I’m feeling about my health with anybody, including my own husband. This app provides me the outlet to share not only my symptoms, but my feelings about my symptoms in a way that feels private and protected. Essentially, it is a diary that allows you to track extremely detailed information that can be helpful for any physical, psychiatric, etc.issues and concerns. I highly recommend this above all other symptom tracking apps because all of the other ones that I have tried have not been anywhere near as helpful as this one has. I don’t review things like pretty much ever… But this app really does deserve more credit than it’s given!

author: Unbeelivery

title: Wonderful Application
body:
I haven’t been using this application very long. So, far I like it very much. 

It’s easier to keep track of what I’ve eaten and how much I drink. I just wish there was a way to log other liquids besides water and that the ounces were more flexible in adjustment. 

Sometimes, I drink a 16 ounce glass of Mimosa or lemon water and other times during the day, I might drink an 8 ounce glass of plain mineral water or a 12 ounce mug of tea or hot chocolate.  

That’s why I deducted two stars. There’s no way to adjust between 8, 12, 16, 20 or other liquid ounce measurements or log other liquid types by name. 

I do like being able to keep track of the physical manifestations I experience along with blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, mood, energy levels, sleep and gratitude. Very nice! 

My primary care physician strongly suspects I have a progressive type of MS. I have been wanting an application such as this one to notate everything I mentioned. Now, I can show her and my neurologist what’s going on with me. Hopefully, it will lead to me actually being diagnosed with it before the year ends. 

I wish I had the funds available for the full version of this application. If I had the money, I might get it. 

Thank you for creating this application! If you contact me by email, my name is Karen Tyrell.

author: Gi Wizard

title: Great, not perfect
body: I want an all-encompassing app to keep all my health metrics in one place. I’m too forgetful to carry a physical notebook to write everything down, and I also don’t want several health apps cluttering my phone screen. Bearable is that app. It allows me to track 99% of the things I want to track (and some things I hadn’t thought to track but have been very helpful when communicating with my doctor). It’s extremely customizable. It’s great if you want to track symptoms. I just wish the nutrition section was expanded. I would like to be able to track individual meals rather than general times of day for foods and daily totals for macros. I’d also like to track things like satiety before and after those meals. Right now I have to use the extra notes section to track those things, which isn’t as convenient as a designated tracker but at least makes it still possible. If they integrated a more comprehensive nutrition tracker that let me track individual meals, I would give it 5 stars.
author: Aidan not Aiden

title: Absolutely AMAZING!!
body: This app has helped so so much, I’ve even showed my drs the app and explained it and now they’re recommending it to other patients.. title: Takes some getting used to.
body:
I'm only on my second day and have barely touched the app and they're asking for a review. Do you love it? Do you just love it? Wellllll... I've barely used it so I can't really give an honest or objective review but you asked so here it goes. 

Im currently only using the free version and there's A LOT to unpack. This is a good thing because if I want to track my health, my disease, my symptoms, my moods and/or my medications I want A LOT to choose from. But I'm trying to get used to all this information and what and where to enter. And it's everywhere. Without time or reason. There is much room for improvement here which is why I may not go with the paid version. It needs more coherence and ease of cross reference. 

One example: I took my evening meds and after 2 hours still couldn't sleep so I  got up took another medication. When I went to record it, I can only enter that I took 2 tablets. Not that I took another hours later. I wouldn't want to look back and thinki took double my dose right out the gate. That's not even remotely helpful in tracking symptoms. It's confusing actually. 

I'd like a daily time line to look at maybe like a calendar So I can see what happened with everything throughout the day at a glance and not need to go through all the prompts. Maybe that's in there and I just haven't found it. 

That's the problem with asking for reviews after literally 5 minutes of use... You haven't given me time to appreciate your app.

UPDATE: After a few days I joined the 7day free trial. There’s A LOT to unpack here and while this has potential to be one of the most helpful apps out there, they have a lot of improvement to do to lessen confusion. For example. Listing medications are in paragraph form causing dosing numbers to run together causing confusion when simply listing them line by line would clear that up. They gave a toggle system but you’re not toggling to show the task has been done. Or still needs to be done. A bullet system here might be better. I’m a retired graphic designer so I have much cleaner and cohesive ideas for this. Right now there’s much room for improvement.

title: I ♥️ Lists and Rating Systems
body:
This app (ESPECIALLY for the price: ~$40/yr right now I think?) allows you to do so much and to customize so much. 

If the number of list items seems too many and is overwhelming, you can hide them. One of the absolute best features of Bearable is that you can write in your own items and your own lists, AND you can choose to do them on two types of ranking scales or simply a yes/no. 

For someone with chronic migraine disorder and a complicated slew of other autoimmune symptoms, I really don’t think I could ask for something better than this!! 

I hope more than anything they don’t end up doing the gradual price increases that lead to high prices before you know it, as some of my other apps have done. As it is right now (April 2025), I am so happy for this app as it is.

author: lef07003

title: I replaced 12 apps w/ this ONE app that does it all better & more affordably
body:
I got this app because I’d heard it was good for managing chronic illness. And it very much is! Bearable has already helped me make some correlations that have improved my quality of life— things I wouldn’t have noticed on my own. 

But within this mission lie several functionalities that I was previously using multiple apps to attend to. (And it was becoming unwieldy! There comes a point when you’re spending more time setting up and updating apps than actually living your life, especially if you have some sort of executive dysfunction.) Bearable offers a multitude of functions that other apps offer as their *sole* function (and charge large monthly fees for).

And it is so entirely customizable that you can track all of your health issues in its single interface. Sleep patterns, pain, GI issues, energy, cognition, mood, allergies, heart issues, menstruation or menopause, weight loss, body measurements, hydration, dietary habits and suspected troublesome foods, exercise, autoimmune or eczema flares— anything you want to track, you can, along with potential influencing factors (again, customizable). And if it has a corollary in Apple Health, you can have the entries sync with each other. 

I also really appreciate the optional inclusion of what many other health apps leave out— social and lifestyle factors such as being outdoors (and the weather), time spent with friends/ partner/ family, screen time and video games, alcohol and caffeine intake, and any custom habits you suspect could be having an effect on your overall wellbeing. 

The yearly subscription fee is totally reasonable for this all-in-one bundle of functionality. There is a dedicated subreddit where the developer participates and is very responsive to feedback and suggestions, and where the enthusiastic user base makes it clear that this app has improved the health and lives of countless people. I’m so grateful that I found Bearable.

title: Easy, valuable, worth every penny
body:
The free version is amazing on its own, but I'm a data junkie, so I chose to invest in a year of premium, and I haven't regretted it for a second. The value this app brings is worth every cent. Especially since I got it while it was on sale (which I hear it frequently is) for a very low price.

TL;DR - This app is highly customizable, user friendly, and feature rich. Comes with all kinds of data visualizations, simple AND advanced, for maximum insight without being hard to understand.

Life changing:
- Detailed insights allow me to identify triggers, patterns, and other data that can provide insight on my symptoms. I can see who has the most positive impact on my life, which habits are truly serving their purpose, and whether any new medications are actually improving my symptoms. PLUS I can see which symptom management techniques are most effective, what time of day or day of the week I feel worst, and how my symptoms fluctuate over time. And more!
- The app provides suggestions for the best ways to manage your symptoms and the worst triggers to avoid, based on data from past logs. You can also input your own symptom management strategies for bad days. 
- Built-in (optional) medication tracking and reminders help me stay on top of which meds I take when, and make sure I never miss a day.
- Optional nutrition and water tracking also allows you to stay on top of your health and make sure you're meeting your needs. (I don't personally use this feature, but I can think of a thousand ways this could be helpful for other users.)

Practical upsides:
- User-friendly and easy to understand. I figured it out and set it up quickly.
- VERY customizable to allow the user to measure and track whatever you'd like, going as simple or in depth as your heart desires.
- Customizable reminders for the best times of day that work for you.
- Simple AND advanced data visualization at any time to best suit your needs.
- Low friction; it's so easy and simple to log symptoms that I find myself naturally doing it 5-10 times a day without reminders. Just tap a button and you're golden. 
- Community focused developers who take suggestions from the users and work hard to make the app better and better. Public suggestion forum includes information on plans for future changes.

Cons:
- Mood is rated on a scale of 1-10 and can be logged as many times per day as you'd like, but other symptoms are rated 0-4 and only up to 4 times per day in time blocks that are not customizable. I personally only care to rate my energy levels in detail, so I was able to work around this by just using the mood tracking section for energy levels instead. But this could be an issue for others.
- Due to the small development team, updates and new features may be slow.
- Does not currently have a built-in menstrual cycle tracker. (But it may in the future?)

THESE OPINIONS ARE MY OWN. I am not being paid or otherwise rewarded to say this.

title: Lots of potential but not quite there
body: I have been using this app every day for 4 months now. It has been ok for keeping track of things (although I’d like to track my symptom onset time with more specificity than 6 hour blocks), but not great for insights. First of all, their correlations grid does not give correlation values, and while that probably doesn’t bother most people, the results and conclusions can be misleading. Also, the 6 hour blocks in which things are tracked make it impossible to discover / distinguish for example migraine symptoms vs. migraine warning signs vs. migraine triggers because I don’t know in what order they happened, just that they all happened in “MID”. The data will still be good for analyzing other larger daily patterns though, like whether my migraines are related to allergies. ~~ I finally downloaded all my data to analyze it myself, and discovered there’s no way to get *all* of your data because it doesn’t export when you marked a symptom as “none” (even they know that unmeasured is not the same as 0, which is why their “Insights” analysis page encourages you to mark symptoms as none when they’re not active instead of leaving them blank). I tried to ask about how to get all of my data using the “Ask support” button under FAQs, but the button doesn’t work. I tried to report this as a bug, but it turns out the “Report a bug” button doesn’t work either 🤣

title: Life saver!!!
body:
I LOVE this app!!! It has seriously made keeping track of my laundry list of health problems so much easier. It’s also helped me improve other areas of my life that I didn’t anticipate when I first downloaded the app, I feel so much more aware and on track with the things in my day to day life. My lifestyle habits have improved, I am able to keep track of everything my doctors need, and I have found correlations in my habits and health that have made me more aware/able to improve my health! Aside from that, it has taken SO much stress out of my health tracking due to it being easy to use, insightful, and reliable. I would recommend this to anyone looking to improve their well being! 

The only reasons I gave this app 3 stars are;

1) The app isn’t the best when you are stuck behind a paywall. After paying, the app is stellar! I just hate subscriptions though and I wish I could pay once and be done with it. I don’t mind paying to support the creators of such a great app, it’s just not ideal that I am going to need to budget over $30+ for this for years. Considering that it’s a yearly payment instead of a monthly, that does help! However, as a girl on a tight budget, it’s not the easiest for me. 

2) This app doesn’t include menstrual cycle tracking, which would be SOOOO incredibly useful! My cycle/hormones have a BIG affect on my other health problems. It’s hard to keep track of the correlations between my health problems and where I am at in my cycle, and it would save me a lot of time if Bearable had a cycle tracking section that could show insights and correlations to/with everything else I track in the app. I use Stardust instead for cycle tracking (awesome app btw) but it is time consuming and somewhat difficult to go through each app and dig through entires to find correlations. I would feel much better about paying for this app if it included cycle tracking (especially since it affects around 50% of the populations health).
author: Kennedy Orange

title: Sadly Cannot Enjoy

I was in and out of the hospital and my stepsister downloaded it for me to help with my CHF symptoms… wasn’t able to keep track of cancelling it and im out my money. I was unable to get a refund. Really steep cost for a time where everything counts. Wish someone could help

Even without the subscription this app is amazing and worth downloading. It would be nice if they could add a widget for the iPhone home screen or lock-screen.
